title: Non-blocking findings from PR #405's review (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups)
description: Tracked follow-up for two non-blocking findings raised in pr-reviewer's review of PR #405 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups), which documented an explicit convention for importing from `src/` in an e2e spec. The convention itself is sound, correctly placed, consistent with the rest of Testing.md, and the one spec (daily-homework.spec.ts) it was written to cover already conforms -- grepping the whole of frontend/tests/e2e/ confirmed no other spec imports from src/ at all, so nothing in the current tree violates the newly-written rule on day one. Neither finding below blocks the accept.

checklist.step: The new convention ("a type, or a pure, side-effect-free utility/formatting function") is documentary only -- there is no `eslint.config.js` rule (e.g. a `no-restricted-imports` override scoped to `tests/e2e/**` allowing only `import type` plus a specific named-export allowlist) that would mechanically catch a future spec importing a React component, hook, or context from `src/` in violation of the rule. The worked example (DailyHomeworkOut as a type, formatDate as a pure function) and the explicit prohibition give a reasonably clear bright-line test for the common case, but "pure, side-effect-free" for a borderline helper (one that calls other src/ functions transitively, does memoization, or has a non-obvious dependency) is something only a human reviewer can judge -- there's no automated backstop today. Worth considering whether a scoped eslint override is practical, and if not, at least noting in Testing.md that enforcement is review-only.

Minor documentation-accuracy nit in the new Testing.md paragraph: it says the exception works because "both `tsconfig.app.json` and Playwright's own `tsconfig` already include `src` and `tests` together" -- but there is no separate Playwright-specific tsconfig file anywhere in `frontend/` (confirmed: no `tsconfig.e2e*`/`*playwright*tsconfig*` file exists, and `playwright.config.ts` doesn't reference one). Playwright's own test runner doesn't type-check specs at all (it transpiles via esbuild without checking types); type-checking of `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` happens solely through the project's ordinary `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` step against `tsconfig.app.json`, which already lists `src`/`tests`/`.storybook` in its `include`. The parenthetical should be reworded to not imply a second, Playwright-specific tsconfig exists -- e.g. "the one `tsconfig.app.json` (via its project-reference build) already covers both `src` and `tests`, so nothing extra needs wiring for either static type-checking or the Playwright runner's own transpilation."

decisions.decision: Added a scoped `no-restricted-imports` override in `frontend/eslint.config.js` (files: `tests/e2e/**/*.ts`) that flags a non-type (value) import from `src/components/**`, `src/features/**`, `src/pages/**`, `src/api/**`, `src/theme/**`, an app entry point (`src/App*`/`src/main*`), or `src/index.css`, while allowing a type-only import from anywhere under `src/` (via the rule's `allowTypeImports` option) and leaving `src/utils/**` completely unrestricted for both type and value imports -- rather than leaving the convention purely documentary, or trying to approximate "pure, side-effect-free" with something more elaborate.
decisions.rationale: A partial-but-useful rule is worth adding here: the mechanizable part of the convention is squarely 'no component/hook/context/page/API-client/theme value import from src/', and ESLint's own (non-deprecated, built into eslint@10's core no-restricted-imports as of this version, not the separate @typescript-eslint wrapper) `patterns` + `allowTypeImports` option expresses exactly that distinction without any custom rule code. I rejected two alternatives: (a) a single `group: ['**/src/**', '!**/src/utils/**']` negation pattern, which I actually tried first and verified empirically (via a small Node script exercising the underlying `ignore` package directly) does NOT work -- gitignore-style negation can't re-include a path inside a directory that's already matched by a broader ignore pattern, so `!**/src/utils/**` silently failed to un-block `src/utils/format` under `**/src/**`; listing the blocked directories explicitly (components/features/pages/api/theme/entry points) instead of trying to negate out of a catch-all avoids that trap entirely. (b) a fully-general 'is this import from a pure function' check, which isn't expressible in ESLint without executing/analyzing the imported module's body (far beyond a lint rule's reach, and the task's own framing agreed this isn't mechanizable) -- so I didn't attempt it; a borderline case (a `src/utils/` helper that's quietly grown an impure transitive dependency) still requires human review, same as before, and the new paragraph in Testing.md says so explicitly. I verified the rule fires on a constructed temporary violating import (a value import of a component from `src/features/homework/`) and does not fire on either of the two legitimate imports already in `daily-homework.spec.ts` (the `DailyHomeworkOut` type import and the `formatDate` value import from `src/utils/format.ts`), then removed the temporary file. `yarn lint` passes clean across the whole frontend tree after the change, confirming no existing file outside `tests/e2e/` is affected by the new override's `files` scoping.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Leaving the convention documentation-only (the 'well-reasoned decline' option the task explicitly allowed) was the main alternative; rejected because the mechanizable subset turned out to be both real and simple to express once I'd confirmed ESLint's built-in `allowTypeImports` option (not a hand-rolled type-detection hack) could do the type/value distinction, and because the false-positive risk this task worried about (forcing eslint-disable comments) proved low in practice: the blocked-directory list is narrow and unambiguous (components/features/pages/api/theme/entry points), and the one genuinely gray area -- whether a `src/utils/` helper is truly pure -- is exactly the part left unrestricted and still deferred to human review, so there's no new disable-comment pressure anywhere a legitimate import would plausibly want to go.

comments.summary: Verified independently: backend (pytest, 99.95% cov, 1655 passed), frontend (vitest, 99.78%/99.06% stmt/branch cov, 1083 passed), ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean, profit-target wording guard clean, validate_tasks.py clean, make e2e 28/28. Re-tested the new no-restricted-imports eslint override myself with different violation shapes than task-worker's own check (value imports from src/api/client and src/pages/DailyHomeworkPage, plus a mixed import with an inline `type` qualifier alongside a value specifier from the same blocked path) -- all correctly flagged; a pure all-inline-type import from a blocked path, and the two existing legitimate imports in daily-homework.spec.ts, correctly pass clean. Confirmed no path aliases exist that could bypass the directory-based matching. Confirmed the Testing.md doc correction is factually accurate: no tsconfig.e2e*/playwright-specific tsconfig file exists anywhere in frontend/, playwright.config.ts references none, and tsconfig.app.json's own include (`["src", "tests", ".storybook"]`) is the sole source of static type-checking for tests/e2e/*.spec.ts via `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (Playwright's own runner only transpiles via esbuild, confirmed by the project's own prior documentation of this and by inspecting playwright.config.ts directly).

Non-blocking: the rule is a directory allowlist (components/features/pages/api/theme/entry-points), not an exhaustive block of everything-but-src/utils. A value import from any src/ directory NOT on that list -- most notably a future src/hooks/ or src/contexts/ (neither exists in the tree today, confirmed) -- would pass the eslint rule silently even though it's exactly the kind of component/hook/context import the underlying Testing.md convention prohibits. Verified this gap empirically: a constructed src/hooks/useFoo.ts (a real React hook, `useState`) imported as a value into a temporary e2e spec produced zero eslint errors. The new Testing.md paragraph documents one real limitation of the mechanized check (a src/utils/ helper that's quietly grown an impure transitive dependency) but doesn't mention this second, more clear-cut one -- a brand-new top-level src/ directory bypasses the check entirely until the allowlist is updated to include it, not just a borderline judgment call. Doesn't block this accept (the rule is explicitly scoped as a partial backstop, and today's tree has no such directory to miss), but worth tracking so the gap doesn't go unmentioned indefinitely.

review.notes: Full review per pr-reviewer process: checked out PR #414, re-ran backend+frontend coverage, static-verify (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc + profit-target wording guard), validate_tasks.py, and make e2e (28/28) -- all clean, matching task-worker's claims. No UI-facing change in this PR itself (docs + eslint config + task-board bookkeeping only, no application source touched), so no interactive browser walkthrough was performed; the persisted e2e suite was still run per step 9a since it's cheap and the PR's own change (a lint rule governing e2e specs) is adjacent to that suite. Independently re-verified the new eslint override with violation shapes different from task-worker's own test (src/api/, src/pages/, and a mixed type+value import) and confirmed both the Testing.md tsconfig correction and task-worker's checklist items are accurate. code-review skill was dispatched (forked/background execution) against the diff but its async result did not return within this review session; given the diff's small, low-risk scope (doc wording, a single eslint config addition, task-board bookkeeping -- no application source code), I performed an equivalent manual correctness pass myself: read the full diff, traced the eslint rule's matching semantics, and empirically tested it (including the one real finding below) rather than relying on inspection alone. One new non-blocking finding surfaced (the directory-allowlist's false-negative surface for a future src/ subdirectory not on the list) and is tracked as a follow-up task rather than left only in this comment.
